title: Sanko plant_lookup_v1 legacy mappings
notes: Original citations, language labels, and collection locations were not retained in the flat runtime file. These mappings remain available for backwards compatibility but require source review.

title: Ethnobotanical survey of medicinal plants used in the treatment of animal diarrhoea in Plateau State, Nigeria
notes: Ethnoveterinary survey. The runtime index uses only the published name mappings and plant parts, not the reported therapeutic use.

title: Which Plants for What Ailments: A Quantitative Analysis of Medicinal Ethnobotany of Ile-Ife, Osun State, Southwestern Nigeria
notes: The published tables are retained in surveys/quarantine for auditability, but excluded from all generated mappings because the publisher retracted the article.

title: Ethnobotanical Survey of Local Flora Used for Medicinal Purposes among Indigenous People in Five Areas in Lagos State, Nigeria
notes: The runtime index uses the inventory's published vernacular mappings and parts, not the locality-by-locality therapeutic-use claims in Supplementary Table S2.

title: Ethnobotanical survey of anti-asthmatic plants in South Western Nigeria
licence: open access; article-specific reuse terms not stated in the PDF
notes: The article reports herbarium identification, but Table 1 does not publish per-row voucher identifiers. Therapeutic claims are retained only as source context and are not exported to the runtime lookup.

title: Ethnobotanical Studies of Port Harcourt Metropolis, Nigeria
notes: All 84 displayed rows are preserved, but production export is blocked pending language and data review. The article states 83 species; the table has an extra unnumbered Acanthus row, and the Neem row appears to swap its common-name and botanical-name columns.

title: Ethnobotanical uses of plants in Nigeria: an analysis of current research trends and patterns
notes: Table 2 is retained as a catalogue of 79 original studies to acquire. Table 3 is retained as secondary review evidence only and cannot produce runtime mappings.

title: Medicinal Plants in Tropical West Africa
source_locator_scope: Botanical and general index, printed pages 355-367
notes: Retained for botanical, synonym, pharmacology, and bibliographic checking. The book does not provide a structured language-labelled vernacular index, so no local-name mappings were inferred from its prose.

title: Handbook of African Medicinal Plants, Second Edition
notes: Only concise mapping facts and page locators are staged. Runtime export is blocked because most vernacular labels lack a row-specific country or locality and have not been reviewed by language practitioners.

title: Sanko practitioner-confirmed vernacular mappings
notes: Local names Sanko could not place botanically, reviewed and confirmed by a named practitioner or the research team through scripts/plant-review.js. Each entry carries a pseudonymous reviewer reference and the number of times the name was seen in use; the source transcripts stay out of this file and out of the repository. This is the only plant source whose evidence is a practitioner's own statement rather than a publication, which is why it is ingested under its own status rather than as 'included' alongside the surveys.

title: Europe PMC and Crossref primary-source discovery
licence: index metadata only; each candidate carries its own licence
notes: Written by scripts/discover-sources.js. A ranked list of Nigerian ethnobotanical sources to acquire, and the resolution of the 79 original studies catalogued in anumudu-2025-nigeria-review to DOIs, licences and full texts. Candidates are citations, not data: no row here produces a vernacular mapping, and an acquired source only becomes ingestable when it is registered in this file in its own right.

title: Wikidata taxon labels in Nigerian languages
notes: Written by scripts/import-wikidata-vernaculars.js. Labels are crowd-sourced and unsourced — no locality, no collector, no citation — and a large share of those returned in an African language are the botanical or English name filed in the wrong language. They are candidates for review, never mappings. A candidate reaches the runtime index only through practitioner confirmation, attributed to the reviewer who confirmed it and carrying the candidate source it came from.
